2 RNA candidates in global field trials
Marks transition from lab to real-world testing, a key step toward commercialization.
Trials in U.S., Brazil and Asia
Targets major row-crop regions; broad agronomic validation can speed market entry.
Addresses high-cost pests like fall armyworm and diamondback moth; large revenue potential.
Candidates met/exceeded standard chemistries in prior stages, de-risking efficacy.
Stability/controlled release may improve field performance and resistance management.

This is a mid-stage R&D milestone in FMC’s biologicals push, moving assets from controlled tests to broad field trials. A larger catalyst would be positive, replicated field data and regulatory paths that signal launch timing, markets, and revenue potential.
